video_title: LeBron Is Still in Awe of Kyrie Irving's Game

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Horford and Brook Lopez's ability to reinvent their games
quotes.excerpt: a guy like Horford has reinvented himself. A guy like Brook was a post player early in his career
quotes.quote: Let's look at Brook and Horford in two different ways. Those are guys that have adapted. They are not like Steph, they are not like you in the Houston series last year, like KD, that are still if you squint you are like that's the same guy. You can still see it, even though we know it's a little bit less picking your spots, business decisions. But a guy like Horford has reinvented himself. A guy like Brook was a post player early in his career, the analytics changed, became a three-point shooter, rim protector.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash breaks down how Brook Lopez and Al Horford successfully reinvented their games to stay effective as they aged in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: Growth mindset as the key to player longevity and adaptation
quotes.excerpt: one word I always talk about is just growth mindset. You look at Brook and you look at Al

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: Talk a little bit about how some of those guys have been able to reinvent and have the big impacts.

text_blocks.speaker: LeBron James
text_blocks.text: One word I always talk about is just growth mindset. You look at Brook and you look at Al, those guys just have a growth mindset to be able to reinvent themselves. There was a time obviously when Al was in Atlanta, you get a switch on him, you throw the ball in the post, he's going to punish the small. And the same with Brook, Brook was a low post threat, you can give it to him multiple possessions in a row and he would make a play. For them to just have a growth mindset and seeing the way the league has changed over time and them to still be able to be on the floor and still make plays in a different role and still be effective, it's a commend to them, it's a tribute to them on just having that growth mindset and being able to still adapt. Adaptability is very key in our league if you want to stick around, and those guys have done it.

quotes.social_post: LeBron James credits the longevity of veterans like Al Horford and Brook Lopez to having a growth mindset and the ability to adapt their roles as the league changes.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Horford's resilience and discipline after injury-plagued seasons
quotes.excerpt: it is a maximum respect for again the discipline, the intelligence, the self-awareness to adapt
quotes.quote: You can easily get played off the floor with the speed of the game. For Al, I thought Al in those Boston teams, he obviously hit five, six threes in the play-in game last year after having a very injury-plagued season. It is a maximum respect for again the discipline, the intelligence, the self-awareness to adapt. There are a lot of ways to get it done.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash praises Al Horford for his discipline and intelligence, noting how he has successfully adapted his game despite injury-plagued seasons.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul George's self-awareness regarding his role in winning a championship
quotes.excerpt: he realized that if he was going to win a championship he couldn't be the best player
quotes.quote: Paul George had a quote a few years ago saying that he realized he was still playing at a high volume, high efficiency, that he realized that if he was going to win a championship he couldn't be the best player on the team, meaning he needed to be second or 1A. That self-awareness is so undervalued and appreciated.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash highlights the importance of self-awareness in stars, pointing to Paul George's admission that he realized he might need to be a second option to win a championship.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on the lack of self-awareness in professional sports
quotes.excerpt: I don't think we have that enough in sports actually, or in life

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: You see that in a lot of everyone, not just Paul.

text_blocks.speaker: LeBron James
text_blocks.text: I don't think we have that enough in sports actually, or in life. We talk about sports, but in life, just being self-aware of not what you're capable of because he's not saying that he's not capable of being the best player on any given night, but the self-awareness saying that I think where I'm at in this point of my career, if I'm the highest usage guy on a team or I'm shooting all the balls or if I'm the main everything, then I don't believe that that's the best ingredients to win a championship. That's commendable to anybody. I shout out PG for that for sure.

quotes.social_post: LeBron James gives a shout out to Paul George for his self-awareness, noting that being the highest usage player on a team is not always the best ingredient for winning a championship.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: The stigma against vulnerability and asking for help in sports
quotes.excerpt: in today's world where in sports you're not allowed to show no vulnerability

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: It's a little bit like vulnerability is strength.

text_blocks.speaker: LeBron James
text_blocks.text: Yeah man, but we're taught not to be vulnerable as athletes. And I already know he probably got killed for saying it too. And I don't even remember him saying that, but like yeah, and especially in today's world where in sports you're not allowed to show no vulnerability, you're not allowed to show like okay, I'm not able to do this, I need help. Everyone gets killed for that. I know it firsthand. But that's commendable. I don't remember him saying that clip, but that's awesome.

quotes.social_post: LeBron James discusses the stigma against vulnerability in sports, saying that athletes are often criticized for admitting they need help or showing weakness.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving's enduring skill level and movement at age 34
quotes.excerpt: Kyrie, 34 and a half. He's the youngest of the games, but he's knocking on the door
quotes.quote: Kyrie, 34 and a half. He's the youngest of the games, but he's knocking on the door of that generation. Early signs are he's moving just like he always did. I saw that preseason game that he played in versus Houston and he looked really good in that preseason game, looked very spry, still had all the stop and goes, the stop on a dime, the one-legged runners. Seems pretty comfortable.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash says Kyrie Irving is still moving as well as he ever has at age 34, noting he looked very spry in his preseason action.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving as the most skilled player in NBA history
quotes.excerpt: Kyrie's maybe the most skilled player to ever play our game
quotes.quote: I feel like Kyrie's maybe the most skilled player to ever play our game, just the breadth of skills, handling, shooting from all angles, finishing. But I think what makes him really special is one of the best movers. We think of athletes in our league as guys that are just dunking on everyone, but his quickness, his change in direction, deceleration, his ability to control his body in air whether it's shooting or finishing, special, special athlete.
quotes.social_post: Steve Nash calls Kyrie Irving the most skilled player to ever play in the NBA, citing his unique combination of ball handling, shooting, and body control.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on Kyrie Irving's incredible shot against the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: he like jumped and he like moved the ball and then PG was like behind him

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: There's one clip that we can bring up in post-production and show it. I believe it was Dallas, Luka's last year there maybe, in the playoffs versus the Clippers. And Kyrie made a move to the basket and they put it in slow motion and he like jumped and he like moved the ball and then PG was like behind him and he like moved it again and finished over both of them.

text_blocks.speaker: LeBron James
text_blocks.text: You got we got to pull this clip. It's in slow motion. I was like, how in the fuck did he make this? And I don't even know why I'm saying how in the fuck because I've seen it for three years being his teammate. So like, but still, when you see it every day, I'm like, oh wow, that was incredible. So yeah, he's the most most skilled I've ever seen and I've watched a lot of basketball and played a lot of basketball.

quotes.social_post: LeBron James says he is still amazed by Kyrie Irving's skill, recalling a playoff finish against the Clippers that left him wondering how Kyrie possibly made the shot.
